description: Our team is looking for motivated teens eager to grow in AI/ML who already have solid experience participating in hackathons and launching digital products. Through this hackathon, we will also gain valuable hands-on knowledge in space and engineering research
summary: Hefest is a Super Intelligence (SI) powered platform that transforms decades of NASA Physical Science Informatics (PSI) microgravity combustion data into actionable fire safety intelligence for deep-space missions. Designed for aerospace engineers and ECLSS designers, Hefest evaluates flammability risks in next-generation exploration atmospheres—including the oxygen-enriched, low-pressure conditions of the Artemis Lunar Base (34% O2, 8.2 psi) and Mars transit habitats. The platform features an empirical SI risk calculator, comparative habitat benchmarking, an interactive flame physics simulator, and life-saving terrestrial spinoffs.
details:
1. The Problem

In space exploration, buoyant convection disappears, creating spherical, diffusion-limited flames that pool toxic gases locally. Furthermore, new Artemis lunar habitats use exploration atmospheres (34% O2 at 8.2 psi) where materials ignite dramatically faster. Until now, valuable NASA flight data (BASS, Saffire, FLEX, ACME) was scattered across research papers without an operational engineering tool.

2. How Hefest Works

- Habitat Benchmarking: Compares environmental risks across the ISS, Artemis Lunar Base, Mars Transit, xEMU spacesuits, and pressurized rovers.

- NASA PSI Flight Catalog: Interactive indexing of flight combustion experiments with direct links to NASA reports.

- Empirical SI Risk Calculator: Computes Limiting Oxygen Concentration (LOC) and flammability margins against NASA-STD-6001B.

- Flame Physics Simulator: Visualizes the physical transition of flame shape from 1g down to 0g microgravity.

- Terrestrial Spinoffs: Demonstrates practical applications on Earth, including fine water mist suppression and submicron smoke detection (SAME).

3. Target Audience

Aerospace systems engineers, ECLSS and fire suppression designers, academic researchers, and students.
